diagram_candidates.excerpt:
For $0<r,s<1$, the Hartogs figure $H(r,s)$ is the union of a thin inner cylinder ...
$$ H(r,s)=\{ |z_1|<1,\ |z_2|<s\}\cup\{ r<|z_1|<1,\ |z_2|<1\}. $$
diagram_candidates.reason: The defining set is a union of two cylinder constraints. In modulus coordinates it has a simple planar footprint, and the missing top-left corner makes the union and its later hull relation much easier to see.
diagram_candidates.content_to_draw_or_check: Axes |z1| and |z2| from 0 to 1; mark r and s; shade [0,1)×[0,s) and (r,1)×[0,1); distinguish the excluded corner [0,r]×[s,1); label open boundary edges accurately. Do not imply pointwise membership at excluded boundaries.

diagram_candidates.excerpt: Given ... $\Lambda=\mathbb Z\omega_1+\mathbb Z\omega_2$ ... square schema ... $a\,b\,a^{-1}\,b^{-1}$. The square map is $g(s,t)=q(s\omega_1+t\omega_2)$ and respects the side pairings.
diagram_candidates.diagram_kind: TikZ lattice fundamental parallelogram and quotient-edge identification
diagram_candidates.reason: The quotient proof repeatedly translates between a lattice in C, its fundamental parallelogram, and a square with paired sides; a diagram can make the quotient map and deck translations explicit.
diagram_candidates.content_to_draw_or_check: Draw a generic positively oriented parallelogram spanned by ω1,ω2; label opposite sides a/a⁻¹ and b/b⁻¹ with directions matching the boundary word aba⁻¹b⁻¹; show lattice translates and q:C→C/Λ; mark g(s,t)=q(sω1+tω2) on [0,1]². Do not assume orthogonal/equal-length generators.
